light-and-bright.name: Light & Bright
light-and-bright.title: Light & Bright — MT. PEAK · Himalayan Black Tea
light-and-bright.metaDesc: Light & Bright — an unoxidised single-origin speciality tea (SFTGFOP-1 CL) from eastern Nepal. Greenish leaf with fine white tips, a light-orange cup, very floral with little astringency.
light-and-bright.desc: A speciality tea graded SFTGFOP-1(CL): greenish leaf shot through with fine white tips. Left entirely unoxidised, it pours a light orange cup — very floral, with a fresh aroma and only the faintest astringency.
light-and-bright.homeDesc: Greenish leaf with fine white tips, left entirely unoxidised — a light-orange cup that is very floral and fresh, with only the faintest astringency.

tasting.v: Fresh and floral, with a clean, high-grown lift.
Light and floral over fine white tips — bright, with only a whisper of astringency.
Clean and fresh, softly floral to the last.

brewSteps: Warm a porcelain or glass pot with hot water, then discard.
Measure 2 grams of leaf for every 180ml of water.
Pour water at about 90°C — just short of a rolling boil.
Steep 3 to 4 minutes, then pour off completely.

make.d: Two or three leaves and a bud, taken by hand.
12–16 hours on the trough, cool and warm air as needed, until the leaf turns supple.
10–20 minutes, breaking the cell walls to set an even shape and texture.
No fermentation step — which keeps the leaf greenish and high in natural polyphenols.
15–20 minutes at 110–120°C, finishing at 3–5% moisture so the leaf keeps.

light-and-bright.originLead: High on the southern slopes of the Himalaya, above the cloud line, the garden grows slowly in thin, clean air.
originPs: Light & Bright is picked in the first weeks of spring, when the leaf carries the brightness of the new season. Cold nights and altitude force it to grow slowly — concentrating aroma, sharpening flavour, and giving the cup its luminous, floral lift.

Every leaf is certified organic, plucked by hands that have read these slopes for generations, and finished at our own factory. No middlemen. Only the mountain, the leaf, and the people who tend both.

spec.v: Two or three leaves and a bud · by hand

light-and-bright.closerP: £68 for 100g of single-origin, hand-plucked Himalayan speciality tea — greenish leaf, fine white tips, a light and floral cup.

mountain-green.name: Mountain Green
mountain-green.title: Mountain Green — MT. PEAK · Himalayan Green Tea
mountain-green.metaDesc: Mountain Green — a single-origin green tea from eastern Nepal, hot-air fixed to keep its colour. Fresh and vegetal with subtle grassy notes. Cultivars T-78, P-312 and Tinali.
mountain-green.desc: A light, delicate green tea from the varieties T-78, P-312 and Tinali. Fixed with hot air within minutes of plucking so it never oxidises — fresh and vegetal, with subtle grassy notes and a sweetness that runs from smooth to gently astringent.
mountain-green.homeDesc: Light and delicate, fixed with hot air so it never oxidises — fresh and vegetal, with subtle grassy notes and a clean, gently astringent sweetness.

meta.v: Spring flush, hand-picked and fired same day

mountain-green.tastingH: A fresh, vegetal cup with grassy notes

tasting.v: Fresh and green, with a subtle grassy note.
Light and delicate, vegetal and grassy, sweet and smooth over a gentle astringency.

brewSteps: Warm the vessel briefly — green tea is unforgiving of heat.
Measure 2 grams of leaf for every 180ml of water.
Cool the water to 80–90°C to keep the leaf from turning bitter.
Steep 2 to 3 minutes; a second, shorter infusion is often the sweetest.

make.d: One or two leaves and a bud, spread on the net in cool air for 15–30 minutes.
Hot air at 120–125°C for up to two minutes, halting the enzymes and holding the green.
Cooled on the net in moving air to keep the natural colour and fresh aroma.
Lightly rolled by hand into a well-twisted leaf.

mountain-green.originLead: Above the cloud line, where the air thins and the nights turn cold, the leaf grows slowly and stays green.
originPs: Mountain Green is fixed with hot air within minutes of plucking — no oxidation, no waiting. What reaches the cup is the closest thing to the living leaf: fresh, vegetal and faintly sweet, the way the garden tastes at first light.

Every leaf is certified organic, plucked by hands that have read these slopes for generations, and finished at our own factory. No middlemen. Only the mountain, the leaf, and the people who tend both.

spec.v: One or two leaves and a bud · by hand

mountain-green.closerP: £74 for 100g of single-origin, hand-plucked, hot-air-fixed Himalayan green tea — fresh, vegetal, unmistakably alive.

golden-harvest.tastingH: A ripe, fruity cup with a honeyed edge

tasting.v: Ripe and fruity, with a warm note of mountain honey.
Round and fruity, mellow and honey-sweet over fine golden tips.

brewSteps: Warm a porcelain or glass pot with hot water, then discard.
Measure 2 grams of leaf for every 180ml of water.
Pour water at a full boil, around 100°C.
Steep 3 to 5 minutes to draw out the honeyed, fruity character.

make.d: One tender leaf and a bud of the Gumti and AV2 varieties, taken by hand.
12 hours on the trough, cool and warm air as needed, until the leaf turns supple.
30 minutes, breaking the cells to release flavour and aroma and set the twisted shape.
12–15 hours at room temperature, watched closely as the colour and aroma develop.
15 minutes at 115–120°C, arresting oxidation at 3–5% moisture.

golden-harvest.originLead: At the peak of the season, when the tips turn gold, our pickers choose only the very best of the garden.
originPs: Golden Harvest is our most generous tea — fully oxidised, deep in colour, honeyed in the cup. Every tip is selected by hand at the height of the season, then carried through a full, careful oxidation to bring out its warmth and depth.

Presented in a hand-finished gift box, it is built to be given as much as brewed. Certified organic, single-origin, and finished at our own factory — no middlemen, only the mountain and the hands that tend it.

spec.v: Fully oxidised black tea · golden tips
One leaf and a bud · by hand
